chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Rabati, from Zakariyya al-A'war, who said:

I saw Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) praying while standing, and beside him was an elderly man who wanted to stand up, and he had a staff of his own. He wanted to reach for it, so Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) bent down while he was still standing in his prayer, handed the staff to the man, and then returned to his prayer.
ai.seo_question: Does bending down to hand something to someone invalidate the prayer?
ai.summary: Note: The chain of narration (isnad) cites Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Ribati and Zakariya al-A'war, who are companions of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), making this a narration of Imam al-Sadiq rather than Imam al-Rida. The incident highlights the concept of 'sujood al-tanazul' (bowing down) while standing, demonstrating that minor, non-disruptive movements for a valid need do not break the continuity of prayer. This serves as a practical precedent for flexibility in ritual posture, emphasizing that the essence of worship remains intact despite necessary physical adjustments.
